How the club rebuilt its academy in three seasons

Long read

Three seasons ago the academy had not produced a first-team regular in almost a decade. The new director started by cutting the number of age groups in half and moving every coach onto a full-time contract, so the people who taught the players were no longer squeezing sessions in around other jobs.

The second change was the pathway. Instead of loaning teenagers to clubs where they rarely played, the club now places them with two partner sides that have agreed to field them every week, and a staff member watches every match. Minutes, not reputation, decide who comes back.

The results arrived faster than anyone expected. Four graduates started in the league this season, and the club sold one of them for a fee that paid for the new training pitches twice over. The director insists the sale was never the point, but admits it made the next budget meeting easier.
